subject.title: test harness: changed-run routing skips active-memory tests; unit lane double-runs gateway packages; forceRerunTriggers drift; orphan configs

question: Should this protected issue land as one coordinated harness refactor, or should routing correctness land first with cleanup and stall-policy follow-ups?
rationale: The defects are source-confirmed, but the report crosses distinct ownership and policy surfaces: project routing, matrix performance, watch triggers, dead tooling, dependency migration, wrapper consistency, and process timeout behavior.

options.title: Split correctness first
options.body: Land active-memory routing, gateway de-duplication, and Docker lane coverage first, then track cleanup and timeout policy separately.

options.title: One coordinated refactor
options.body: Centralize all lane metadata and complete every reported cleanup in one owner-reviewed change with broad matrix proof.

recommendation.title: Split correctness first
recommendation.body: Land active-memory routing, gateway de-duplication, and Docker lane coverage first, then track cleanup and timeout policy separately.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and repeatedly maintained the central scoped Vitest and extension-routing architecture and authored this protected report.
